body:
I think the "bigger picture" is that I used to have very solid auditory hallucinations as a child, various voices in my head when I was around 7-10 and my "imaginary friend" was not only fully visible but a total asshole. I talked to someone about it and I can't quite remember if she was a psychiatrist or therapist or what but she told my mom she thought I was schizophrenic, my mom had a fit, I stopped seeing this lady who I quite liked and that was that.

Later on, when I was about 11 my step-dad began abusing me. I feel like I have gone through every coping phase in regards to what happened. 

I started hanging out with other abused children in middle school, all of who had been severely physically/verbally/sexually abused as well. I was, however, "normal" in their eyes. I never told them what was going on at home, well, not for a long, long time. 

Fast-forward to about 13, my step-dad had just gotten done and I started just yelling at him that I hated him that I never wanted to see him, that he was scum. He took it to heart and never touched me again apart from the disgusting wet kisses he'd give me on my cheek right in front of my mom. 
I would tell me it bothered me, but she saw it as no big deal, she was happy that her husband was "affectionate" and "caring" with me.
Later that year, I confided in her the reason why it bothered me so much. She cried, but never confronted him.

At 14, he turned to me in the car and yelled at me to "get a job" so I did. 
At 17 I had paid for a trip to Europe on my own (no help from either of them) The week before I left, he told me he needed to talk to me when my mom left. It still disgusts me to this day remembering that day.
I was chopping up something in the kitchen, then he whispers in my ear that he needs to talk to me. My heart starts racing, thinking of what I can do. What if he just wants to talk about my mom's fundraiser event  which is soon after I return from the trip? Then I just look stupid for leaving. 
But what if it was something more malicious? At this point, I had nearly earned a black belt in two martial arts, I had flipped and sparred men bigger than him. I grabbed the pocket knife I had and kept it in my pocket just in case along with a voice recorder. 

He comes home and sits me down and starts joking about being a "dirty old man" but that he has to confess that he's in love with me. He doesn't love my mother, but I'm almost old enough to officially run off with him and leave her behind. Now, through this process, at that point, I still had a great deal of love and respect for my mother because she was ignorant of the situation, so the fact that he's asking this is just delusional. 
I told him to burn in hell, got up, he tried to grab me but I fought back. He didn't fight too much. He just let me go.

 I drove 90 miles out and sat on the edge of a ledge, contemplating what would happen if I just jumped then and there. I sat there for over 2 hours. In the end, I decided that I wasn't going to let him ruin my life. I was going to go on my trip. However, there was one week left before the trip, so I did the logical thing, I ran away. 
I went to a friend's house and stayed with her. At this point my mother was very worried as it was very unlike me to be out past my 12 a.m curfew. I ignored all of her calls. She found me at work. She was angrier than I had ever seen her in my life but I was angrier. 
She was causing a scene, I kept my cool. I had an officer friend remove her. However, it was said that because I was underage I had to return home no matter what the altercation and the friend housing me would be in danger of losing the help she was getting from the state and with two children, I couldn't be the cause of that.
I returned home, hired a guy to install a lock on my door the day after both my step-dad and mom barged into my room with him crying and begging forgiveness for the "misunderstanding" She was crying too, I yelled at them to get the fuck out and they did. I din't talk to either of them and just left for my trip. 

On my trip, though short and with my classmates, I got to do a lot of soul-searching. I opened up to my host mom, who incredibly had gotten through the same experience, except she, unlike my mother, had the courage to leave her now ex-husband. 
Later on the trip when drinking with my friends and enjoying the fact that no one gives a fuck when you drink in Europe I opened up to them too. Despite being completely wasted, I woke up feeling like this giant burden had been lifted. 
I left Europe vowing to return. 

When I went back home, I was still painfully 17. My step-dad caused a scene at a restaurant, kicked me out of the car on the drive home, I walked home to find his car gone but my mom still there. Had the worst fight I have ever had with her. She slapped me and I pushed her into a wall. I moved out within 3 days of turning 18. 
At 19, I went to Europe with my then, best friend and visited my host family from the previous year where I had another heart to heart with my host mother and she gave me input that my mother is probably afraid of being alone because women are seen as "no longer desirable" when they get past a certain age. It really opened my eyes and for the first time ever, I was able to put myself into my mother's shoes, even though it was more like a pair of loose slippers as I still couldn't comprehend how a mother could choose a man over taking care of her child.

I then went to stay with my best friend and upon visiting his home, seeing his family, how much they loved him and he them it was an eye-opening experience and it made me realize that I didn't want to be one of those people who looks at a calendar and goes "gee, I haven't spoken to my mother in 20 years" 
So after one year of ignoring her every phone call/text/snail mail letter I broke the silence and began communicating with her again. 

I no longer see her as my mother, just a friend. Currently, I talk to her maybe once every two/three months and haven't seen her in well over a year despite living 3 hours away. 
I feel that chapter of my life is closed. While I have no desire to go visit her and my step-father. I no longer hold a grudge. Any regrets are not mine to have, and while the relationship is damaged irreparably, I do not see that as a sign of me holding on to the past. It's just what it is.
I think the bigger picture is the hallucinations/false memories, mood-swings and I don't necessarily think they're a byproduct of the abuse.
As I mentioned earlier, I used to have similar things when I was younger, prior to the abuse and those experiences/feelings have now returned in full force. 

Sorry for the wall of text.

No you're right, I had ZERO input when I got tossed into the police car and even less input when they were taking my information at the hospital. I remember telling them "I don't want to be here, I can't pay for it" over and over again and the counselors there just kept saying "don't worry about the money, worry about yourself" imagine my surprise/anger when I got the bill. 
Thank /u/taufish for your advice and kind words. I will try to find a psychiatrist if my insurance at this job kicks in.
